From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Leadership Group <leadership@redwood.com>; Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 02 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hiring tradeoffs & OKR impact: Q4 -> Q1 scenario planning

Team —

Putting this in your inbox as we start QBR prep. We need a short prioritization decision on headcount that balances: (a) finishing Q4 commitments, (b) protecting critical Q1 launches, and (c) near-term cost discipline. Rough ask: come back with an itemized set of reqs/backfills to approve or defer by EOD Nov 6.

Quick context: our current hiring plan assumes +45 hires through Q1. Macro pressure means we should consider a constrained plan (~+25) and a set of carve-outs (CS/Prod-eng/backfills for critical ICs). I attached the org_headcount_model_2025_v2.xlsx with scenarios (tabs: baseline / constrained / carveouts).

Please do two things:
- By Tue (11/04) mark each open req as: APPROVE / DEFER / EXCEPTION (must include rationale and expected OKR impact).
- Flag any backfill that if delayed would materially increase risk to a committed delivery (call out feature/release and owner).

I'll consolidate and propose a decision meeting on Nov 6 (time below) unless objections.

Proposed decision slot: Thu Nov 6, 10:00–10:30 PT (Leadership sync).

Thanks —
Neha
Neha Kapoor
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: org_headcount_model_2025_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Leadership Group <leadership@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 02 Nov 2025 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hiring tradeoffs & OKR impact: Q4 -> Q1 scenario planning

Thanks Neha — this is timely. Two quick framing notes (to keep the decision clean):

1) Prioritization framework: protect hires that are both (i) directly tied to revenue/expansion OKRs and (ii) unblock critical launches with definable metrics.
2) For backfills: differentiate between a) technical ICs on active release branches (high risk if delayed) and b) junior growth ICs (lower immediate impact).

I'll start tagging reqs in the sheet with my initial calls. My quick proposals:
- Protect product-eng backfills for the inference runtime squad (they're on the critical release path).
- Defer two early-stage hiring pipelines (intern conversion and entry-level infra) pending cluster-usage savings review.

Note: we should surface any region/locale constraints (we have a few EMEA hires that are revenue-facing; those may be higher urgency).

On the meeting: Nov 6 10:00 PT works for me. If we need a quick pre-read, I can circulate a 1-pager Tuesday afternoon.

—Jonas

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hiring tradeoffs & OKR impact: Q4 -> Q1 scenario planning

Agree with the framing. Two operational asks from me:

- Please add a short column: CONSEQUENCE IF DEFERRED (one sentence) for each req. We need to be able to tell Finance/CEO the impact succinctly.
- Exceptions process: any req marked EXCEPTION must route to me + People Ops with a 1-paragraph justification and an alternate mitigation plan. No exceptions without a mitigation.

I've attached a quick priority_ranking_20251102.csv with my recommended top 15 line-items (mix of backfills and 3 strategic hires). If something is not on the list but is critical, flag it with "EXCEPTION" and copy People Ops.

Markus
Head of Eng

Quick notes inline:

> Protect product-eng backfills for the inference runtime squad (they're on the critical release path).

+1 on protecting runtime backfills. If we delay those, the latency/QoS improvements tied to the Q1 partner launch slip.

> Defer two early-stage hiring pipelines (intern conversion and entry-level infra) pending cluster-usage savings review.

Agree on defer for intern conversion hires — low near-term OKR impact.

Operational ask: Customer Success has two open roles tied to SLAs for top-5 customers (renewal conversations scheduled late Nov). I recommend we carve those out as APPROVE — losing them increases churn risk and has direct revenue implications.

I can consolidate the final proposed list and circulate a pre-read Tuesday evening (11/05) for the Nov 6 call.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Hiring tradeoffs & OKR impact: Q4 -> Q1 scenario planning — Decision & action items

Thanks everyone — brief recap and decisions from today's call (attached approved_reqs_20251106.xlsx and decision_notes_20251106.pdf):

Decisions (approved / deferred / exception):
- APPROVE: 7 reqs (product-eng backfills x3; runtime infra engineer x1; CS SLA hires x2; one Sr SRE tied to autopatcher)
- DEFER: 15 reqs (intern conversions, entry-level infra roles, two non-critical PMs)
- EXCEPTION: 3 reqs (strategic marketplace biz-dev hires) — require written justification + Markus approval + People Ops sign-off

Action items:
- People Ops: start offers for APPROVE set and prioritize comp approvals (owner: People Ops)
- Hiring managers: update consequence-if-deferred column in the sheet for deferred reqs by Mon Nov 10 (owner: respective managers)
- Markus: triage EXCEPTION packets and provide decisions by Nov 12
- Finance: model the constrained scenario in the shared drive (owner: Finance FP&A)

Notes: we prioritized revenue-facing and delivery-critical roles. We also agreed to re-open the plan in two quarters if macro improves.

If you have edits to the approved list, route them as a follow-up email to me + People Ops (no direct offer changes without People Ops).

Neha
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: approved_reqs_20251106.xlsx (spreadsheet); decision_notes_20251106.pdf (PDF)
